resources.string: Your habits, one commit at a time.
A repo is a habit you choose. A commit records progress toward its target, including partial progress.
Start with an empty workspace on this device. No account or connection is needed. Your optional profile and preferences live in Settings.
Your workspace has no habits or commits. Create a repo to start recording your own progress.

GitHabit keeps your workspace on this device, without accounts or cloud sync. Uninstalling erases local data. Exports are plaintext and a chosen document provider may sync them independently. Import is not yet available in this build.
A name and note for this device only. Leave either blank or clear them at any time.
Changes save when selected. System follows the device appearance.
Active weekly bridge: %1$s–%2$s (inclusive). These dates are fixed.

Save to change the calendar. Existing and current periods stay intact. Short bridges are unscored for weekly quotas; daily and selected-weekday habits continue normally. Stored progress never moves to a different date.
This workspace has no dated history. Saving applies the choice immediately.
Saving cancels only the pending request. Effective history and any active bridge stay fixed.
Check the device date before changing the calendar.
The local date is now %1$s. Review the projected dates, then save again.
Save habits and history as plaintext JSON.

This replaces all local repos, commits, profile, and preferences with an empty workspace. Export first to keep an external copy. A verified preservation copy is required before replacement; external exports are not deleted.
Try another filter, or start a new intention.
Open a repo from the list to inspect its progress and history.
Name your habit, enter a daily target and unit, then choose when to reach it.
Reach the daily target on every active day.
Choose at least one weekday. Other days remain optional.

resources.string: The daily target and unit above apply to each qualifying day. Multiple commits on one date count as one day, not extra days or a total weekly quantity.

This habit change applies on the date shown, not next week. The resulting partial week is transitional and unscored, not a success or failure. All progress and earlier expectations stay intact. Settings → Week starts on is separate and takes effect at a future boundary.
